findings.title: Team admin/owner permission check uses `&&` instead of `||`
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. Because `isTeamAdmin` checks `role === "ADMIN"` and `isTeamOwner` checks `role === "OWNER"`, a single membership cannot satisfy both conditions unless `isTeamAdmin` also accepts `OWNER` (and even then, `&&` restricts it to owners only, blocking team admins). It should use `||` so that either a team admin or a team owner is permitted to add guests.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials
findings.body: `addGuestsHandler` allows an attendee or team admin/owner (who may not be the booking organizer) to add guests, but lines 158–163 instantiate `EventManager` with `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. When an attendee or another team admin calls this endpoint, `EventManager` will try to update the calendar event using the caller's credentials rather than the organizer's (`booking.user`), causing the calendar update to fail or target the wrong account.

findings.title: Duplicate emails in `input.guests` and case-variant emails bypass deduplication and blacklist checks
findings.body:
`uniqueGuests` only filters against existing `booking.attendees` and `blacklistedGuestEmails` using exact case-sensitive string comparisons, and does not deduplicate within `input.guests` itself:
1. If a client calls the tRPC procedure directly with `guests: ["a@b.com", "a@b.com"]` (since `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` does not enforce uniqueness), duplicate attendee rows will be created.
2. `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased on line 71, but `guest` is not lowercased before `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` or before comparing with `attendee.email`, so `User@Example.com` bypasses both the blacklist and existing-attendee checks.

findings.title: Raw `guests` array passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead of filtered `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the unfiltered `guests` input rather than `uniqueGuests`. If `guests` contains an email that was already an attendee on the booking (filtered out of `uniqueGuests`), `sendAddGuestsEmails` will match `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` for that existing attendee and send them an `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`.

findings.title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores event type `disableStandardEmails` metadata settings
findings.body: Other email manager functions (such as `sendLocationChangeEmails` and `sendScheduledEmails`) accept `eventTypeMetadata` and check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` before sending emails to the host or attendees. `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not check these flags, so adding guests will send emails even when standard emails are disabled on the event type.
